headline: French Blood Stores Report No Loss After Cyberattack
deck: EFS says altered refrigeration settings at three plasma cold-storage sites were detected before blood products or samples were compromised.
body: French authorities said a cyberattack tried to raise temperatures to extremely high levels at several blood banks, but it was stopped before it damaged blood products or samples. [E1]

The French Blood Establishment said temperature and defrosting thresholds were raised to extremely high levels on Monday at three plasma cold-storage sites; its monitoring systems detected the problem and staff acted before products or samples were compromised. CBS News also reported EFS’s account of the raised thresholds at three sites. [E2] [E4]

No health consequences had been identified and no blood products were lost. [E3] The paper reported on 5 November that EFS monitoring and alarm systems identified anomalies and enabled measures to ensure that no samples or blood products were altered. [E5]
